why: THE FIX DID NOT HOLD. This trouble was cleared 2026-08-05 (cairn e87c386, ticket validation-store-door-is-the-only-path) with three physics layers. On 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08 — two and three days after that clear — two voyages wrote SIX validation trails around the door anyway. Seven entries across six trails carry no trail_link, and persist_validation is the only hand that mints one. The chain (layer 2) recorded the evidence and is the only layer that worked; nothing READ it, so the breach sat undetected for eight days and surfaced only incidentally, when harbor_master.clearance consulted one of those trails during an unrelated crossing on 2026-08-15.

occurrences.what_wrote_them: run_proof's output, written to the file by a hand that was not the door. Measured from shape: every one of the seven carries EXACTLY the ratified eight fields and exactly run_proof's evidence keys (returncode, stdout_tail, stderr_tail, seal, source_fingerprint) — the door's minted trail_link is the only thing missing. Five of the seven landed inside 66 seconds (17:16:50 -> 17:17:56), i.e. one loop over five proofs.

why_each_layer_missed_it.layer_1_mode_bit: TWO INDEPENDENT HOLES. (a) It cannot protect a file that does not yet exist: 3 of the 7 entries are entry 0 of a trail file created in the same commit, so there was no 0444 to defeat. (b) For the other 4 — appends onto existing 0444 trails — the mode bit stops only a naive open(path,'w'). Any writer that replaces the inode by rename walks past it, and that is the DOOR'S OWN technique: the clearing note says so in its own words, 'The door still writes because os.replace needs the DIRECTORY, not the file.' A hand imitating the door's method inherits the door's exemption.
why_each_layer_missed_it.layer_2_chain: WORKED — and is the only layer that did. It recorded the absence faithfully and refused to let a verdict be read out of the trail. But nothing reads the chain corpus-wide, so the record sat unread for 8 days; it took an unrelated crossing consulting ONE trail to surface it. Detection was incidental, not designed.
why_each_layer_missed_it.layer_3_corpus_scan: Censuses every MODULE for a write aimed at a validations/ address. An ad-hoc throwaway script is not a module in the corpus, so it is invisible to the scan. Note the ORIGINAL occurrence (2026-07-30) was also 'an ad-hoc sealing script' — the same shape, and the layer built afterward does not cover it.

occurrences.the_report_named_the_closing_fix_and_the: This trouble's own the_fix_when_taken listed option (b): 'run_proof persists through the door itself, closing the handoff rather than guarding it.' The 2026-08-05 fix guarded the handoff instead of closing it, and run_proof's docstring still reads 'does not persist it (the store is a later stone)'. The recurrence came through exactly that unclosed handoff — the caller must still choose the sink, and twice now a caller chose the file.
occurrences.recoverability: NOTHING TO RECOVER. Measured per entry with git log --follow: each of the seven arrived unlinked at its first commit and carries no trail_link at any commit. The clearing note's stated recovery path ('git is the recovery path, and the chain is what tells you to use it') does not reach this class: it recovers a DESTROYED trail, and nothing here was destroyed — these entries were never linked in the first place.
occurrences.second_finding_riding_this_one: adopt_chain CANNOT TELL THIS FROM PREHISTORY. Its docstring is emphatic that it is 'not a repair tool and deliberately not usable as one', but its guard refuses only an entry whose EXISTING link fails to verify. A MISSING link passes straight through, so pointing adopt_chain at any of these six trails would silently mint links over a post-door bypass and erase the evidence — precisely the outcome the docstring says it exists to prevent. The distinguisher between 'unadopted prehistory' and 'written around the door' is the DATE (adoption ran 2026-08-05; these are 08-07 and 08-08) and nothing in the function reads it. A date floor would close it.
occurrences.mode_bit_census_expected_not_new: 89 of 90 trails on disk are 0444; cairn/tools/base/validations/test_nest.json is 0664. This is ALREADY PREDICTED by the clearing note — 'git carries only the exec bit, so a fresh clone lands these files at 0644 and the mode-bit layer is absent until the door next appends' — so it is expected residue rather than a new hole. Recorded here so the next reader does not re-derive it, and left untouched deliberately: chmod by hand would be a hand applying physics.

occurrences.the_fix_when_taken: Not designed here (this reports, it does not design). Weighing, cheapest first: (a) a corpus-wide chain census as a standing tooth or probe, so a break is found in minutes rather than 8 days and by design rather than incidentally — this is the layer that was missing, since layer 2 detected everything and told nobody; (b) a date floor on adopt_chain so it refuses an entry newer than the adoption itself, closing the second finding; (c) run_proof persists through the door itself, which is the option this trouble named in 2026-07-30 and which was not taken — it closes the handoff instead of guarding it, and both occurrences came through that handoff. (a) and (b) are cheap and independent; (c) is the one that ends the class.

recurred_after_clear.what_changed: cairn e87c386, ticket validation-store-door-is-the-only-path. The declared single write-door is now the only path by physics, in three layers, each answering a different failure mode. (1) MODE BIT: _atomic_write drops a written trail to 0444, so the exact bypass recorded in this ticket — v.write_text(json.dumps(rec)) from an ad-hoc script — now raises PermissionError at the open() instead of destroying 17 seals silently. The door still writes because os.replace needs the DIRECTORY, not the file. (2) CHAIN: every record carries a trail_link minted by persist_validation and by nothing else (a caller-supplied link is refused), a sha256 over the whole trail beneath it plus the record itself; standing() verifies before reading any verdict and refuses the whole trail on a break, so harbor_master clears no crossing on a trail written around the door. This is what answers the sentence at the heart of this ticket — a hand-write no longer looks exactly like a fresh seal. (3) CORPUS SCAN: a proof tooth censuses every module for a write aimed at a validations/ address, so a second writer reds on arrival rather than after it has run. The 73 pre-existing trails were adopted (220 entries linked, all verify); adoption refuses to re-link a tampered trail. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND IS NOT CLAIMED FIXED: the bytes remain writable to a caller running as the same uid, nothing here can un-destroy a trail (git is the recovery path, and the chain is what tells you to use it), and git carries only the exec bit — so a fresh clone lands these files at 0644 and the mode-bit layer is absent until the door next appends. The chain is the half that survives a clone. Proven: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_validation_store.py 9/9 (6 new teeth, including both halves of the ticket falsifier — the naive write cannot land bytes, and the forced write cannot pass for a seal), test_quorum 9/9, corpus at 86 proofs · 85 green · 1 red over four consecutive runs.
